clue.text: Multitude not well accommodated in Jerusalem

indicators.note: what is accommodated is given room inside a house, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: Zion is the hill of Jerusalem and a poetic name for the city
someone not well is sick

explanation.surface: Crowds of pilgrims in Jerusalem struggle to find lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: Zion is the biblical name for Jerusalem, taken from the hill on which the city stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A zillion is an informal word for an indefinitely huge number, so a vast crowd or host.

clue.text: For extremist to laze is wrong

indicators.note: words that are wrong are not in their right order and must be put straight

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A moral claim that idleness is a sin, in the eyes of a fanatic.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is a fanatical, uncompromising follower of a cause, so an extremist.

clue.text: Skirt, unlike pants, is very tight

definitions.note: a cryptic description: a skirt, unlike trousers, has no legs

blocks.note: first meaning: pants (American trousers) have legs, a skirt does not
second meaning: tight is slang for drunk, and this is slang for blind drunk

explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to be about clothes fitting closely, but 'tight' means drunk. Legless is British slang for too drunk to stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless describes a garment without legs, and also, in British slang, someone so intoxicated they cannot stand.

clue.text: Embarrassed about article. I will rally

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer words wrap the article

blocks.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
a is the indefinite article
to rally someone is an old word for teasing or banter

explanation.surface: A shy writer, awkward about a piece they wrote, promises to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rally' looks like a recovery but is its older sense of mocking good-humouredly; the article sits between the other two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill at ease is an idiom for feeling uncomfortable or awkward, as an embarrassed person does.

clue.text: Bill covering huge amount gets on top of somebody destitute

indicators.note: a thing covering another surrounds it on both sides
in a down entry, one part placed on top of another comes first in the grid

blocks.note: neb is a bird's bill or beak
as in costing the earth, a vast sum
one is a person, someone

explanation.surface: A huge bill lands on a penniless person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like an invoice, which suits the surface; it is a bird's beak, split to wrap the huge amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Near the bone can mean living with almost nothing to spare, impoverished, as when money is cut to the bone.

clue.text: Leader, overdrawn, cut back

blocks.note: an overdrawn account is in the red
Il Duce, 'the leader', was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: A boss whose bank account is overdrawn has to economise.
explanation.walkthrough: No word signals the insertion: the commas simply set the leader within the overdrawn colour. Il Duce, Italian for 'the leader', was Mussolini's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Reduced is a past participle meaning made smaller or trimmed, just as spending is cut back.

clue.text: Spirit manifested in military exercises

indicators.note: what is manifested in something shows itself within it, sitting inside the words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Fighting spirit shown by soldiers on manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' reads as morale, but it is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a whiskey distilled from rye grain, and whiskey is a spirit.

clue.text: Research reveals letter enclosing meal ticket

indicators.note: a thing enclosing another wraps around it

blocks.note: dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
LV is a luncheon voucher, a British meal ticket given to workers

explanation.surface: An investigation turns up a letter wrapped around a lunch voucher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meal ticket' usually means a source of easy income; here it is a literal luncheon voucher.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig deeply into a subject to investigate it, i.e. to research.

clue.text: Copper's arresting sailor who's raised weapon

indicators.note: in a down entry, something raised is turned to read upwards
arresting someone means holding them, so one part is held inside another

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the apostrophe S
an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A policeman arrests a sailor who has brandished a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is a police officer in the surface but the metal in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short, curved, broad-bladed sword once favoured by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: In end. Sir Patrick is exempt

indicators.note: the preposition places the named knight inside the other word

blocks.note: to die is to come to an end
Sir Patrick Spens is the doomed sea captain of a Scottish ballad

explanation.surface: A verdict that Sir Patrick is finally let off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish ballad Sir Patrick Spens tells of a sea captain drowned on a winter voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense someone from a duty is to release or excuse them from it, which is to exempt them.

clue.text: Get rum keg clean with a sponge

indicators.note: rum is old slang for odd or peculiar, so the letters come out in a strange order

blocks.note: taken as written
the article added to the mix

explanation.surface: An instruction to scrub out a rum barrel using a bath sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink in the keg, but it is the anagram signal; 'sponge' is the cake, not the cleaning tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel cake is a light, airy kind of sponge cake made with whipped egg whites.

clue.text: Meditative position that induces languor

blocks.note: first meaning: the cross-legged posture used in yoga and meditation
second meaning: the fruit of Homer's ...-eaters, which made them dreamily idle

explanation.surface: A yoga pose so relaxing it leaves you drowsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is both a seated yoga posture and the mythical fruit in the Odyssey that made sailors forget home.

clue.text: Part of New Testament contrarily included in Old, it's clear

indicators.note: contrarily means the other way about, so the book's short name runs backwards
something included in another thing sits within it

blocks.note: OT stands for the Old Testament
Rev is the abbreviation for Revelation, the last book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A Bible scholar notes that a New Testament passage, turned about, appears plainly in the Old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' pairs with 'New Testament' in the surface, so it is read as OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, the opposite of hidden, so clear.

clue.text: Devil mostly holding the stage with mild character

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
a thing holding another grips it inside itself

blocks.note: the Tempter is a name for Satan
a stage in history is an era

explanation.surface: An actor playing a devil in a quiet, restrained performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The stage' suggests the theatre, but it is a period of time, held inside the devil once his last letter has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate describes climate or temper that is moderate and free from extremes, i.e. of a gentle nature.

clue.text: Hi-fi equipment from Nashville, say

blocks.note: first meaning: a combined home stereo unit
second meaning: a city famous as the capital of country music

explanation.surface: Stereo gear made in Tennessee.
explanation.walkthrough: Music centre is a British term for an all-in-one hi-fi with record deck, radio and cassette.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashville, Tennessee is the heart of the country music industry, an example of a city devoted to song.

clue.text: Totally secure? Not enough for little pigs

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for something completely safe
second meaning: in the fairy tale the three little pigs' houses were blown down by the wolf, so a house was no safety at all

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a joke: being only as safe as a house would not have saved two of the three little pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom describes anything perfectly safe and certain, typically a sound investment or a sure bet.

clue.text: 11 needs back to play better

blocks.note: the answer to 11 across
the rump is the hind part or backside

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that needs a backing piece to win the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 points to the answer at 11 across, OVERT. 'Back' is a body part, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games, to overtrump is to play a higher trump card than one already played, beating it.

clue.text: Rudely leap in and be coarse

indicators.note: done rudely means done roughly and without care, knocking the letters about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Barging in uninvited and being vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rudely' fits the bad manners of the surface, so it reads as plain description rather than the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plebeian originally meant of the Roman common people, and now means lacking refinement, vulgar.

clue.text: Tried to reflect changes in bank's authority

indicators.note: changes here is a verb: the preceding words alter their arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, all three words

explanation.surface: A bank adjusts its rules to take account of recent reforms.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter of credit is a bank's written undertaking authorising payment to a seller on a buyer's behalf.

clue.text: Trade in cars etc

blocks.note: first meaning: to deal or trade, often illegally, as in drugs
second meaning: the vehicles moving on roads

explanation.surface: A dealer in motor vehicles and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the motor trade; 'in' is just a joining word between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic means commerce or dealing, and also the vehicles moving along roads collectively.

clue.text: Like Don's home, housing Soviet policeman

indicators.note: a building housing someone holds them within its walls

blocks.note: someone at home is in
Lavrenti Beria was Stalin's secret police chief

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman's house gives shelter to a Soviet police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don's home' looks like the definition, but the definition ends at 'Don's': a don is a Spanish gentleman, and home is IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberian refers to Spain and Portugal, so it describes things belonging to a Spanish nobleman.

clue.text: Each one gets the bird making an entrance

indicators.note: something making an entrance comes inside, into the other word

blocks.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
pie is an old name for the magpie

explanation.surface: A performer gets jeered on coming on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Each one' looks like a single phrase, but only 'Each' is the definition. 'Gets the bird' is theatre slang for being booed.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece is an adverb meaning for each item or person, as in 'a pound apiece'.

clue.text: Club engineers support

blocks.note: a brassie is an old name for a golf club, the number two wood
RE are the Royal Engineers of the British Army

explanation.surface: A society of engineers backs a project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' reads as a verb, but it is a noun naming an undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is a woman's undergarment designed to hold up the breasts, a kind of support.

clue.text: Stalk as support

blocks.note: first meaning: to walk stiffly and proudly
second meaning: a bar or brace in a framework

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalk' suggests the stem of a plant propping up a flower, but it is the verb for a proud walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Strut is a verb for walking with a swaggering gait and a noun for a structural brace.

clue.text: Port left by an idiot

indicators.note: a place left by someone no longer contains them, so those letters go

blocks.note: Antwerp is a major Belgian port
taken as written; these letters depart

explanation.surface: A harbour abandoned by a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTWERP loses its opening AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is an informal word for a silly or contemptible person, a fool.

clue.text: Conclude there's no escaping hell

indicators.note: what escapes gets out, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: taken as written; these letters leave
the Inferno is hell, as in Dante

explanation.surface: A grim verdict that nobody gets out of hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No escaping' reads as 'impossible to escape'; instead, NO escapes from the end of INFERNO.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence, so deduce or work out.

clue.text: Prominent old boy with unusual virtues

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters fall into a different order

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
taken as written

explanation.surface: A distinguished former pupil known for rare good qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prominent' fits the old boy in the surface, but it defines the answer, which means sticking out unpleasantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtrusive means sticking out or noticeable in an unwelcome way, as a prominent structure may be.

clue.text: I was first, they say

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so it is the pronunciation that counts

blocks.note: someone who was first won the race

explanation.surface: Someone boasting that they came first, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker; it is the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman numeral I stands for the number one.

clue.text: It takes nerve to match what American wears with suit

blocks.note: neck is cheek or nerve, as in 'what a neck'
to tie is to draw level or match a score

explanation.surface: It takes courage to keep up with how Americans dress for business.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the garment is just a tie; NECKTIE is the usual American word, hence the definition naming an American.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is the strip of cloth knotted under a shirt collar, worn with a business suit.

clue.text: Stretch of river in which vessels are found

indicators.note: the river is the place within which the other word is found

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A length of river where boats are moored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests boats on the river; they are kitchen pans.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide continuous area or stretch of land, water or sky.
